obligation: Notify actively exploited vulnerabilities in your product to the coordinating CSIRT and ENISA via the single reporting platform: early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within 14 days of a fix.
applies_to: Manufacturers of hardware/software products with digital elements placed on the EU market
article: Art. 14(1)-(2); applies from 11 Sep 2026 per Art. 71(2)

obligation: Notify severe incidents affecting the security of your product to the CSIRT and ENISA: early warning within 24 hours, incident notification within 72 hours, final report within one month.
applies_to: Manufacturers of hardware/software products with digital elements placed on the EU market
article: Art. 14(3)-(5); applies from 11 Sep 2026 per Art. 71(2)

obligation: Draw up a software bill of materials in a commonly used machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies, and identify and document product vulnerabilities and components.
applies_to: Manufacturers of hardware/software products with digital elements placed on the EU market

obligation: Remediate vulnerabilities without delay through security updates (separate from feature updates where feasible), distributed securely and free of charge throughout the declared support period.
applies_to: Manufacturers of hardware/software products with digital elements placed on the EU market

obligation: Put in place and enforce a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy and a public contact address for reporting vulnerabilities in the product and its third-party components.
applies_to: Manufacturers of hardware/software products with digital elements placed on the EU market

obligation: Exercise due diligence on third-party and open-source components and report vulnerabilities found in an integrated component to whoever maintains it, then remediate.
applies_to: Manufacturers of hardware/software products with digital elements placed on the EU market

obligation: Perform and document a cybersecurity risk assessment of the product and apply it across planning, design, development, production, delivery and maintenance.
applies_to: Manufacturers of hardware/software products with digital elements placed on the EU market

obligation: Classify and report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority using the prescribed templates: initial notification, intermediate report and final report.
applies_to: EU financial entities (banks, investment firms, insurers, payment and crypto-asset service providers, etc.)
article: Art. 19; applies from 17 Jan 2025 per Art. 64

obligation: Maintain and update a register of information covering all contractual arrangements for ICT services from third-party providers, and supply it to the supervisor on request.
applies_to: EU financial entities (banks, investment firms, insurers, payment and crypto-asset service providers, etc.)

obligation: Test all ICT systems and applications supporting critical or important functions at least yearly.
applies_to: EU financial entities other than microenterprises

obligation: Run threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) on live production systems supporting critical functions at least every three years, including in-scope ICT third-party providers.
applies_to: Financial entities identified by competent authorities for TLPT (not microenterprises)

obligation: Report significant incidents to the CSIRT or authority: early warning within 24 hours, incident notification with initial assessment and IoCs within 72 hours, final report within one month.
applies_to: Essential and important entities in NIS2 sectors (generally medium-sized and larger)
article: Art. 23(4); Member States apply from 18 Oct 2024 per Art. 41

obligation: Manage supply chain security, assessing each direct supplier's vulnerabilities, product quality and secure development practices.
applies_to: Essential and important entities in NIS2 sectors (generally medium-sized and larger)

obligation: Use multi-factor or continuous authentication solutions and secured communications within the entity, where appropriate.
applies_to: Essential and important entities in NIS2 sectors (generally medium-sized and larger)

obligation: Management bodies must approve and oversee cybersecurity risk-management measures and members must follow cybersecurity training.
applies_to: Essential and important entities in NIS2 sectors (generally medium-sized and larger)

obligation: Authenticate users with multiple factors or continuous authentication for access to network and information systems, with strength matched to asset classification.
applies_to: Cloud, data centre, CDN, managed service and managed security service providers, DNS/TLD, online marketplaces, search engines, social networks, trust service providers
article: Annex, point 11.7; Art. 16 (entry into force 20 days after OJ publication of 18 Oct 2024)

obligation: Report significant security incidents to the joint BSI/BBK reporting office: early report within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within one month.
applies_to: Particularly important and important entities (besonders wichtige / wichtige Einrichtungen)
article: § 32(1) BSIG (applies once the reporting channel is set up); law in force day after promulgation, BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 301 of 5 Dec 2025

obligation: Register with the BSI (name, contacts, public IP ranges, sector, EU countries served, supervisors) within three months of becoming an in-scope entity; report changes within two weeks.
applies_to: Particularly important and important entities and domain name registry service providers
article: § 33(1), (5) BSIG; three months after entry into force on 6 Dec 2025

obligation: Ensure adequate cybersecurity protection for general-purpose AI models with systemic risk and their physical infrastructure.
applies_to: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
article: Art. 55(1)(d); Chapter V applies from 2 Aug 2025 per Art. 113(b)

obligation: Perform and document adversarial testing and model evaluation of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, and report serious incidents to the AI Office.
applies_to: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk

regulation: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) as amended by Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
obligation: Make high-risk AI systems resilient to attacks exploiting vulnerabilities, with measures against data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples and confidentiality attacks.
applies_to: Providers of stand-alone high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
article: Art. 15(5) of Reg. 2024/1689; date per Art. 113(c)(i) as replaced by Reg. 2026/1744

regulation: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) as amended by Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
obligation: Make high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products resilient to attacks exploiting vulnerabilities, including data/model poisoning and adversarial inputs.
applies_to: Providers of high-risk AI systems under Art. 6(1) and Annex I product legislation
article: Art. 15(5) of Reg. 2024/1689; date per Art. 113(c)(ii) as replaced by Reg. 2026/1744

regulation: EU Radio Equipment Directive cybersecurity delegated act (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30, amended by 2023/2444)
obligation: Internet-connected radio equipment must not harm networks or misuse network resources, and must protect personal data, to be placed on the EU market.
applies_to: Manufacturers and importers of internet-connected radio equipment, wearables, toys and childcare devices
article: Art. 1(1)-(2) applying Directive 2014/53/EU Art. 3(3)(d)-(e); date per Art. 3 as amended by Reg. 2023/2444

regulation: UK Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023 (SI 2023/1007)
obligation: Do not ship connectable consumer products with universal default passwords; passwords must be unique per product and not guessable.
applies_to: Manufacturers of consumer connectable products supplied in the UK

regulation: UK Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023 (SI 2023/1007)
obligation: Publish a point of contact for security-issue reports with acknowledgement and status-update timelines, and publish the product's defined security-update support period.
applies_to: Manufacturers of consumer connectable products supplied in the UK

regulation: SEC Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure rule
obligation: Disclose material cybersecurity incidents on Form 8-K Item 1.05 within four business days of determining materiality.
applies_to: SEC registrants other than smaller reporting companies
article: Form 8-K Item 1.05; Section II.I Compliance Dates (non-SRC compliance date)

regulation: SEC Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure rule
obligation: Disclose material cybersecurity incidents on Form 8-K Item 1.05 within four business days of determining materiality.
applies_to: Smaller reporting companies registered with the SEC
article: Form 8-K Item 1.05; Section II.I Compliance Dates (smaller reporting companies, +180 days)

regulation: SEC Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure rule
obligation: Describe in the annual report the processes for assessing and managing cyber risk, third-party risk oversight, and board and management governance of cybersecurity.
applies_to: SEC registrants, for fiscal years ending on or after 15 Dec 2023

obligation: Adopt an incident response program and notify affected individuals within 30 days of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information; oversee service providers, who must notify within 72 hours.

article: 17 CFR 248.30(a)(3)-(5); Section II.F Compliance Period (18 months after 3 Jun 2024 publication)

obligation: Adopt an incident response program and notify affected individuals within 30 days of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information; oversee service providers, who must notify within 72 hours.
applies_to: Smaller covered institutions (broker-dealers, advisers, investment companies, transfer agents)
article: 17 CFR 248.30(a)(3)-(5); Section II.F Compliance Period (24 months after 3 Jun 2024 publication)

regulation: FTC Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information (Safeguards Rule, 16 CFR 314) amendment
obligation: Notify the FTC electronically within 30 days of discovering a security event involving the customer information of at least 500 consumers.
applies_to: Non-bank financial institutions under FTC jurisdiction (e.g. mortgage brokers, auto dealers, tax preparers)

regulation: US FD&C Act section 524B — Ensuring cybersecurity of devices (21 U.S.C. 360n-2)
obligation: Include a software bill of materials covering commercial, open-source and off-the-shelf components in premarket submissions for cyber devices.
applies_to: Sponsors of 510(k), PMA, De Novo and related submissions for internet-connected medical devices
article: Sec. 524B(b)(3); effective 90 days after enactment on 29 Dec 2022 (Pub. L. 117-328 §3305(d))

regulation: US FD&C Act section 524B — Ensuring cybersecurity of devices (21 U.S.C. 360n-2)
obligation: Submit a plan to monitor and address postmarket vulnerabilities including coordinated disclosure, and provide patches on a regular cycle and out-of-cycle for critical vulnerabilities.
applies_to: Sponsors of premarket submissions for cyber devices

regulation: CMMC 2.0 (32 CFR part 170; DFARS Case 2019-D041, 48 CFR part 204)
obligation: Hold a current CMMC Level 1 or Level 2 self-assessment and an affirmation of continuous compliance in SPRS for each system handling FCI/CUI as a condition of contract award.
applies_to: DoD contractors and subcontractors processing FCI or CUI on their own systems
article: 32 CFR 170.3(e)(1) Phase 1; DFARS 252.204-7025/7021; rule effective 10 Nov 2025 (Phase 2 C3PAO start suspended July 2026)

regulation: US Coast Guard Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System (33 CFR part 101 subpart F)
obligation: Submit a Cybersecurity Plan covering MFA, least privilege, asset inventory, network maps, protected logging and encryption to the Coast Guard for approval.
applies_to: Owners/operators of U.S.-flagged vessels, MTSA-regulated facilities and OCS facilities

regulation: California CCPA regulations — Cybersecurity Audits (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, §§ 7120-7124)
obligation: Complete the first independent cybersecurity audit report on the business's cybersecurity program (audit period 2027) and certify completion.
applies_to: CCPA businesses with significant-risk processing and 2026 annual gross revenue over $100M

regulation: California CCPA regulations — Cybersecurity Audits (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, §§ 7120-7124)
obligation: Complete the first independent cybersecurity audit report on the business's cybersecurity program (audit period 2028) and certify completion.
applies_to: CCPA businesses with significant-risk processing and 2027 annual gross revenue of $50M-$100M
